drivingQuestion: What case does the mishna's nine-year-old clause address?
outcomeNote: Difficulty answered in the next unit by Abaye and Rava

segments.he: וּבֶן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְכוּ׳. קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין, בְּשׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם לְבֶן תֵּשַׁע וְיוֹם אֶחָד. לְמַאי? אִי לְמִיפְסַל — קָטָן נָמֵי מִיפְסָל פָּסֵיל, אִי לְאוֹכוֹלֵי — גָּדוֹל נָמֵי לֹא מַאֲכִיל!
segments.en: § It is «also» taught in the mishna that «a nine-year-old» boy disqualifies a woman from partaking of teruma and does not enable her to partake. «It enters our mind» that the mishna is referring «to a widow waiting for her yavam,» who is «nine» years «and one day old.» The Gemara therefore inquires: With regard «to what» is this taught? «If» it is with regard «to disqualifying» her from partaking of teruma, «a younger» yavam «also disqualifies» her, as a levirate bond was created and she cannot return to her father’s house. And «if» it was with regard «to enabling» her «to partake» of teruma, «an older» yavam «does not enable» her «to partake either,» as discussed above.

moves.summary: Assumes the clause concerns a widow awaiting a nine-year-old yavam
Either way the age is irrelevant

edges.about: if the clause concerns a widow awaiting a nine-year-old yavam, it is pointless for both disqualifying and enabling
